exact_statement: For the distinct-Finset version of Erdos 786, let H_N be the hypergraph on {2,...,N} whose edges are supports of disjoint finite subsets with equal products and unequal cardinalities. The original targets are tau(H_N)=o(N) and a coherent infinite density-one construction. In this round, strengthen GC.1 by proving that every sufficiently large N contains a connected family F_N of support-minimal bad relations, all in a fixed top band, with pairwise one-point intersections, matching number one, and transversal number at least 2^(sqrt(log_2 N)/200). Promotion of this scoped theorem counts only as a standalone decisive lemma unless either original target is also closed.
source: P. Erdos, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory (1980), p.114, distinct-elements formulation; read-only predecessor amra-research-loop/campaigns/erdos-786-global-closure-round4-20260824
scope_notes: Variant lock: every relation uses two disjoint finite sets of distinct positive integers; after cancellation coefficients lie in {-1,0,1}.
The fixed top band in the target is (N/64,N]. The factor 64 permits reduction from arbitrary N to the largest power of two at most N.
The quantitative target is uniform for every sufficiently large integer N, not only a sparse subsequence.

The predecessor GC.1 gives only tau>log_2 N on powers of two. This round must obtain a stretched-exponential lower bound while retaining pairwise one-point intersections, matching number one, equal normalized defect, and support minimality.
The scoped lower-bound theorem does not imply tau(H_N)=o(N), an upper bound on tau(H_N), or either density-one assertion.

Public search for an exact solution of Erdős 786 remains prohibited by the predecessor contract; only ordinary background results and priority checks for the final scoped theorem may be consulted after proof reconstruction.
